The report chapters that cover each of the seven tasks are noted in parentheses above. A final task and milestone table for the project is provided in Appendix C. The implementation of data-driven process controls for these five technologies supports DOE EERE’s and IEDO’s mission to accelerate the innovation and adoption of cost-effective technologies that eliminate industrial greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions. GHG emissions reductions are achieved through reduction in electricity including aeration energy for Integration of Data Driven Process Control for Maximizing Energy and Resource Efficiency in WRRFs 5 degradation of organics and BNR (scope 2), reduction in chemicals including methanol for BNR, PAA for disinfection, magnesium chloride for phosphorus (P) recovery, and polymer for dewatering (scope 3), and reductions in direct emissions of CO , N O, and CH from the 2 2 4 wastewater treatment process (scope 1). There are no plans for commercialization of the products from this project. The ML Toolkit is a publicly accessible website. While it targets users in the water industry, it is available to anyone who accesses the site. Providing open access via the ML Toolkit allows utilities to design methods that will work for them. Also, open access provides opportunities for broader involvement in new solutions since the protocols are not locked down and owned by a few. 1.3 Project Innovation and Impact WRRFs underwent an instrumentation revolution over the last 3 decades.
